## Goal

Remove entries from the tracked Pi configuration (`.pi-config/agent/models.json` and any matching `settings.json` patterns) that name models the provider does not actually serve, and canonicalise the ids that only work as undocumented aliases — so agents stop selecting an entry that fails with a 400 at request time.

User story: As a producer, I want the tracked Pi configuration to list only models that the configured providers actually serve, so that a session never fails mid-task because it selected a phantom model entry.

## Evidence (probed 2026-02-08 against live provider endpoints)

Local Proxy — `GET http://192.168.0.199:8000/v1/models` returns `embed, private, plan, author, code, compact`. Chat probes:
- `plan` -> HTTP 200; `compact` -> HTTP 200
- `qwen3` -> HTTP 400 `model 'qwen3' not found`
- `gpt120` -> HTTP 400 `model 'gpt120' not found`

deepseek — `GET https://api.deepseek.com/models` returns `deepseek-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro`:
- `deepseek-v4-pro` -> in catalogue, valid
- `deepseek-v4-flash` -> NOT in catalogue; accepted only as an undocumented alias (HTTP 200 reporting `"model":"deepseek-flash"`). Canonical id `deepseek-flash` also carries correct metadata: contextWindow 1048576, maxTokens 393216, text+image input, effort levels low/high/max

MunitoAI — `GET https://api.munito.ai/inference/v1/models` lists both tracked ids; both valid (no change)

opencode / opencode-go `modelOverrides` — live `GET /models` returns `api_key_expired` (separate credential defect, out of scope). Against the cached catalogue (`~/.pi/agent/models-store.json`):
- `opencode`: `qwen3.5-plus`, `qwen3.6-plus` present -> valid
- `opencode-go`: `qwen3.7-plus`, `qwen3.8-max` present -> valid; `qwen3.6-plus` and `qwen3.7-max` absent -> suspect

## Scope

In scope: `.pi-config/agent/models.json` (tracked), plus `settings.json` `enabledModels` patterns if they reference a removed entry.
Out of scope: expired `opencode` / `opencode-go` API keys (file separately); adding models that are served but not tracked (`compact`, `private`, `embed`) unless the producer asks.

**Key Files:**
- `.pi-config/agent/models.json` — tracked model configuration
- `.pi-config/agent/settings.json` — tracked settings with `enabledModels`
- `scripts/merge_pi_agent_config.py` — merge helper (non-destructive by design)
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — installation script; invokes the merge helper
- `tests/test_merge_pi_agent_config.py` — merge helper tests
- `tests/test_models_config_qwen_thinking.py` — Qwen thinking override tests; asserts tracked overrides exist, so must be updated when ids are removed
- `.pi-config/agent/retired-models.json` — **new** tracked source of truth for pruned ids (see Producer decisions)

## Acceptance criteria

1. `Local Proxy` provider lists no model id that the proxy rejects: `qwen3` and `gpt120` are removed.
2. `deepseek` provider references only catalogued ids: `deepseek-v4-flash` is replaced by `deepseek-flash`, with metadata matching the catalogue (contextWindow, maxTokens, input modalities, effort map).
3. `deepseek-v4-pro` is retained and its **full** metadata reconciled with the catalogue, not only the two known deltas: `contextWindow` 1000000 -> 1048576, `maxTokens` 384000 -> 393216, `input` modalities matching the catalogue, and `thinkingLevelMap` / `reasoningEffortMap` reconciled so a level is not `null` in `thinkingLevelMap` while simultaneously mapped to `"high"` in `reasoningEffortMap`. The catalogue metadata captured by the AC 6 probe is the authority.
4. `opencode-go` `modelOverrides` entries not present in the cached catalogue (`~/.pi/agent/models-store.json`; the live `GET /models` returns `api_key_expired`) are removed: `qwen3.6-plus`, `qwen3.7-max`; entries confirmed present are retained unchanged.
5. `settings.json` `enabledModels` contains no pattern that matches nothing after the change (`pi models` emits no "No models match pattern" warning).
6. Verification is a **one-off command, not a committed script**: (i) each provider's `GET {baseUrl}/models` response diffed against the tracked ids, (ii) the deepseek catalogue metadata for `deepseek-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro` (used to settle AC 2 and AC 3), and (iii) `pi models` showing no "No models match pattern" warning. The exact commands and their captured output are recorded in a comment on this item. No `scripts/` checker is added by this item.
7. **Prune semantics in the merge helper (producer option B).** `scripts/merge_pi_agent_config.py` gains explicit prune support driven by a tracked retired-ids source, and prunes those ids (model entries *and* their `modelOverrides` keys) from the destination while still preserving every **unlisted** local-only provider, model, override and top-level key. After `scripts/install_pi.sh`, `~/.pi/agent/models.json` contains none of `qwen3`, `gpt120`, `deepseek-v4-flash`, `qwen3.6-plus`, `qwen3.7-max`; the prune is reported in the merge summary and a backup is written before the modification.
8. Tests cover the merge/validation behaviour where the repository already has test coverage for `scripts/merge_pi_agent_config.py`.
8a. `tests/test_models_config_qwen_thinking.py` is updated: the `OPENCODE_GO_QWEN` set is reduced to the retained ids (`qwen3.7-plus`, `qwen3.8-max`), and its assertions no longer require `qwen3.6-plus` / `qwen3.7-max` on `opencode-go`.
8b. `tests/test_merge_pi_agent_config.py` covers the new prune behaviour: a retired id present in the destination is removed (both as a model entry and as a `modelOverrides` key); an **unlisted** local-only model/override is preserved verbatim; a retired id absent from the destination is a no-op; a second run is an idempotent no-op (no second backup, no duplicated entries); and the merge summary reports the prunes.

## Producer decisions (recorded 2026-11-17)

1. **Stale-id purge → option B**: extend `merge_pi_agent_config.py` with prune semantics rather than relying on a manual machine cleanup or relaxing AC 7. Proposed mechanism (implementation detail, may be adjusted by the implementer as long as the AC 7/AC 8b behaviour holds): a new tracked file `.pi-config/agent/retired-models.json` maps provider -> retired ids; the merge helper reads it when present, prunes those models and `modelOverrides` keys from the destination, reports each removal in its summary, and keeps preserving everything unlisted.
2. **`deepseek-v4-pro` metadata → reconcile fully** (AC 3): `input` modalities and the thinking/effort maps are reconciled too, not just `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`.
3. **Verification → one-off**: a recorded command and its captured output on this item; no committed `scripts/` checker and no `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` entry.

## Assumptions

- The proxy `/models` endpoint is authoritative for Local Proxy model ids (probe-confirmed by 400 responses).
- `deepseek-v4-flash` -> `deepseek-flash` is a rename, not a second model, because the server reports `deepseek-flash` in the response body.
- opencode-go catalogue validity could not be probed live; the cached store is treated as the best available evidence and will be re-checked if a key is restored.
- The prune is driven by an explicit tracked retired-ids list rather than inferred from the destination, because the destination carries no record of which local entries originated from the tracked config — inference could delete genuine operator additions.

## Impact

Agents can no longer select a Pi model entry that fails with a 400, so sessions stop dying mid-task on phantom models.

## Discovered-from

Operator request: "Remove invalid models from Pi configuration"; prior related items `Add paid minutoai deepseek to the Pi config (SA-0MW0GL4590046BTK)` and `Update tracked models.json to add DeepSeek v4.1-flash-1017 to MunitoAI provider (SA-0MW6RY8O1006M3F2)`.


## Folded scope (2026-11-18): the unservable `MunitoAI/*` pattern

Folded in from `CUR-0MWL0EBP30071E1J` (games_curator), with the producer's explicit approval (Q2 of that plan session = "yes, fold"). The defect: driven child sessions intermittently die at startup with `No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"`, aborting a `drive` chain. Root cause on the configuration side: `MunitoAI` resolves `apiKey` from `$MUNITOAI_API_KEY`, which is absent from the shell/pane environment, so the tracked `MunitoAI/*` pattern in `enabledModels` matches nothing. Reproduced this session: `pi models` prints `Warning: No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"` (exit 0).

This item already owns `.pi-config/agent/settings.json` `enabledModels` pruning, so the fix belongs here rather than in a second item touching the same file and tests. **The live file alone is not enough**: `scripts/merge_pi_agent_config.py` *unions* the tracked `enabledModels` patterns into `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`, so an edit to the live file is reverted by the next merge/install run. The tracked file is the durable source.

**Additional acceptance criteria (folded):**

9. `.pi-config/agent/settings.json` `enabledModels` no longer contains the `MunitoAI/*` glob; the explicit `MunitoAI/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash` entry is retained unchanged (a named id is not the defect — the wildcard is).
10. After a `scripts/merge_pi_agent_config.py` run, `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` `enabledModels` contains no `MunitoAI/*` pattern; re-running the merge is idempotent and does **not** re-add it (union semantics pinned by a test in `tests/test_merge_pi_agent_config.py`).
11. `pi models` emits no `No models match pattern` warning afterwards (one-off verification command and its captured output recorded in a comment on this item, consistent with producer decision 3).
12. `models.json` — including the `MunitoAI` provider `apiKey: "$MUNITOAI_API_KEY"` resolution — and `settings.json` `defaultProvider`/`defaultModel` are unchanged; the edit is scoped to the single `enabledModels` glob entry.
13. The removal is documented as reversible in the merge/install context (which tracked file, which entry, how to restore), so a workflow relying on paid MunitoAI models can be re-enabled deliberately.
14. `tests/test_install_pi_models_config.py` and `tests/test_merge_pi_agent_config.py` cover the absence of the glob (the tests are updated, not weakened).

**Key Files (folded scope):**
- `.pi-config/agent/settings.json` — tracked `enabledModels`
- `scripts/merge_pi_agent_config.py` — union semantics (no behaviour change expected; tests pin them)
- `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` — installed destination (operator-owned; merge output)
- `tests/test_merge_pi_agent_config.py`, `tests/test_install_pi_models_config.py`

**Why no behaviour change is expected in the merge helper:** the pattern is removed from the tracked *source*, so the union simply has one fewer pattern. If the implementer finds the union needs a prune as well, the retired-ids mechanism from producer decision 1 is the place to extend it — but a defensive re-add of a tracked pattern is not a realistic failure mode.

**Related work:** `CUR-0MWL0EBP30071E1J` (the report; also tracks the spawn-classification/retry/release features as `SA-0MWLDZ8ZN0030T15`, `SA-0MWLDZBTF004LJFP`, `SA-0MWLDZFL4006I9YY`, `SA-0MWLDZIS500136UK`).

related: SA-0MWB1H4RF006R7SI (canonical decomposition of the tree-first green-evidence lookup)

## User story

As an operator auditing a work item whose pushed commit the dev-push gate already failed, I want the audit's **red-entry diagnostics** to read the gate's tree-keyed verdict, so a red gate verdict produces the same structured failure diagnostics as a red loose-key entry today — instead of the verdict being invisible and the audit re-executing the whole suite.

## Scope: the residual gap only (duplicate-work reconciliation)

`SA-0MWB1H4RF006R7SI` ("Audit: reuse the tree-keyed dev-push gate verdict for full-suite evidence", stage `plan_complete`) already owns the green-evidence half of this gap with a four-child decomposition:

- `SA-0MWIXIO0R006HL36` — Core: `_classify_full_suite_cache` tree-first query with worktree fallback
- `SA-0MWIXJOBO001SFK8` — Tests: tree-kind hit / legacy worktree hit / different-tree miss
- `SA-0MWIXJ84T000GBWG` — Reporting: surface `fingerprint_kind` and age in audit output
- `SA-0MWIXK8XW003VA3D` — Docs: test-skill-reference and audit evidence documentation

That item's "Desired change" explicitly places `_cached_red_failures` **out of scope** ("red-diagnostics only; a red entry never satisfies evidence and the caller executes fresh"). That is the uncovered gap this item now covers, and only that gap: the green-evidence acceptance criteria of this item's original description are dropped as owned by `SA-0MWB1H4RF006R7SI`. Re-scoped during planning on 2026-11-17 (see the plan comment for the AC comparison).

## Problem

`.githooks/pre-push` and `implement.py finish` bind their full-suite verdict to the pushed commit's **tree** SHA (`run_tests.py --scope full --fingerprint <tree>` → `fingerprint_kind="tree"`, SA-0MW7C6BMZ00931JG / SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4). `implement.py` reads that entry back tree-first (`_full_suite_cache_present`, added by SA-0MWAXC5TD00461FN).

`_cached_red_failures()` (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:4759`) never does this. It calls:

```python
entry = query_cached(command, cwd=str(root), ttl=AUDIT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS)
```

with **no** `fingerprint` and **no** `fingerprint_kind`, so it looks up the loose *worktree* key (`sha256(HEAD + dirty content)`, `compute_git_state` in `skill/test_cache.py`) — a different namespace from the tree key.

Consequences:

- A red tree-keyed gate verdict at the audited `HEAD` is **invisible**: no failure records are parsed.
- `_cached_red_evaluation()` therefore returns `None`, and the audit falls back to the execute-dependent path (a fresh suite run) rather than explaining the failure from the evidence the gate already produced.
- The 24 h `AUDIT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` acceptance window (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81) does not reach gate-produced red runs at all.

## Proposed approach

1. Reuse the tree-resolution helper the core child introduces (`_resolve_audited_tree`, per `SA-0MWIXIO0R006HL36`, mirroring `implement.py`'s `_resolve_commit_tree`). Do **not** introduce a second resolver.
2. In `_cached_red_failures()`, resolve the audited `HEAD`'s tree once, then for each full-suite command query **tree-first** — `query_cached(command, cwd=..., ttl=AUDIT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS, fingerprint=<tree>, fingerprint_kind=FINGERPRINT_KIND_TREE)` — falling back to today's loose-worktree query only on a tree miss (legacy entries).
3. Fail-soft on an unresolvable tree: fall back to the loose query, never raise into the caller (the existing `except Exception` miss contract stays), and never fabricate a failure.
4. Keep the existing filters byte-for-byte: a `scope != "full"` entry is still not red diagnostics (SA-0MT6CEO700058ZEN), and only `exit_code != 0` entries are parsed.
5. Record provenance on each returned failure record (`fingerprint_kind`, plus `tree` when tree-keyed) so a reader can tell a reused gate verdict from a loose-key entry. `_cached_red_evaluation()` consumes the same records — no duplicated lookup logic.
6. Leave `skill/test_cache.py` untouched: `query_cached()`'s worktree-only default (`fingerprint=None`, legacy keying) must stay byte-for-byte for every other caller.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `_cached_red_failures()` consults the tree-keyed entry before the loose worktree key, and a red tree-keyed full-suite entry at the audited `HEAD` yields the same parsed failure records as the identical loose-key entry today.
2. Loose-key fallback is unchanged: a legacy worktree-keyed red entry (with no tree entry) still parses exactly as today.
3. A tree entry recorded for a *different* tree is ignored — a red verdict for another tree is never attributed to the audited `HEAD`.
4. An uncomputable tree (`git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` failure / detached / corrupt) falls back to the loose query only: no crash, no fabricated failure, no unhandled exception.
5. Red diagnostics still flow through the single path: `_cached_red_evaluation()` obtains them from `_cached_red_failures()`, with no second cache query implementation.
6. Each returned failure record carries machine-readable provenance (`fingerprint_kind`, and `tree` when tree-keyed) so a reused gate verdict is distinguishable from a loose-key entry.
7. Changed-scope (partial) entries remain non-evidence for red diagnostics, exactly as today.
8. `query_cached()`'s worktree-only default is unchanged for every other caller (no signature or default change in `skill/test_cache.py`).
9. Tests, executed through the test skill, cover: tree-keyed red hit, legacy loose-key red hit, different-tree ignored, uncomputable-tree fallback — deterministic (no real cache dir, no live git state; prime a tmp cache / stub `query_cached`). Avoid the `test-writing-guidelines.md` anti-patterns (no self-referential simulations, no duplicates of existing core coverage).
10. Docs updated: `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (cache evidence/diagnostics resolution) and `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` § "Legacy and foreign entries miss" so the dual-key lookup is documented where the cache contract lives.
11. Full suite passes.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_cached_red_failures`, `_cached_red_evaluation`, `_resolve_audited_head`, the tree resolver from `SA-0MWIXIO0R006HL36`
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `FINGERPRINT_KIND_TREE`, `query_cached(fingerprint=…, fingerprint_kind=…)` (read-only, unchanged)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_resolve_commit_tree` / `_resolve_post_push_verification` precedent (`SA-0MWAXC5TD00461FN`)
- `skill/audit/tests/` — red-diagnostics cache test home (`test_audit_runner_green_run.py` or a sibling module)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `SA-0MWIXIO0R006HL36` (core tree-first classifier query): it introduces the tree-resolution helper and `FINGERPRINT_KIND_TREE` wiring this item reuses rather than duplicating.

## Notes

- Root cause found while answering "does implement/audit run the full suite, and does push run it again?" — implement and the pre-push hook are correctly tree-keyed and de-duplicated; the audit is the remaining duplicate execution path.
- Do NOT weaken or remove the pre-push gate: it is the fail-closed proof that the pushed tree is the tested tree for pushes that bypass `finish`.
- This item deliberately does **not** change the classifier's green evidence path — that is `SA-0MWB1H4RF006R7SI`'s scope.

## Plan (2026-11-17)

Small item (effort `Small`, risk `Low`): planning pre-check returned `skip`, so no child decomposition. Six automated review stages ran against this content; AC coverage review returned `proceed`; stage advanced to `plan_complete`.

## Impact

A red dev-push gate verdict at the audited commit is visible to the audit's red diagnostics, so audits explain the failure from evidence the gate already produced instead of re-running the whole suite.
data.title: Audit red-entry diagnostics read the tree-keyed dev-push gate verdict

## Goal

The implement-skill reference documents the new spawn-time provider-failure recovery path — the infra retry, the `infra-retry` spawn verdict, the release-to-`open` distinction and the configuration remedy — so an operator can diagnose the failure from the docs and the drive report alone.

User story: As an operator whose drive run stopped, I want the reference to tell me what the `children_driven` entry means and what to fix, instead of decoding `No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"`.

## Context

This item is **F5** of the upstream plan for `CUR-0MWL0EBP30071E1J` (games_curator) and depends on **F2** and **F3** (and on the config fold in `SA-0MWL5AL4B004X0FN`) so the docs describe behaviour that exists.

Existing doc homes to update: the "Drive failure recovery: bounded finish attempts, reconciliation and reset" section (including its verdict table around the `infra-retry` row and the `failed` row) and the "Spawn-failure evidence" section of `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` documents the spawn-time infrastructure retry: which failures are classified, that it reuses `--infra-retry-limit` and its backoff, and that it re-spawns the same child inside the same invocation.
- The verdict/`children_driven` table states that a spawn-time provider retry is recorded as `result: "infra-retry"` with `step`, `reason`, `attempt` and a provider-naming message, and the `failed` row states when the retry is *not* taken (unclassified reason, or a child already reconciled terminal).
- The spawn-failure-evidence section states the two release semantics and why they differ: a killed/timed-out session keeps `in-progress` (so `finish` / `--finalise-stranded` still apply), while a provider failure that never started a session is released to `open` with an empty assignee.
- The configuration remedy is documented (drop the unservable `enabledModels` pattern; the tracked `.pi-config/agent/settings.json` is the durable source because the merge unions tracked patterns into `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`), including how to reverse it.
- The docs-integrity test `tests/test_implement_docs_drive_recovery.py` is updated to cover the new documented statements (a drifting doc fails the suite).
- No code behaviour is documented that the shipped F2/F3 implementation does not provide (cross-checked against the code, not written from this description alone).

## Implementation sketch

1. Read the shipped F2/F3 code, then update the two sections and the table rows.
2. Extend `tests/test_implement_docs_drive_recovery.py` with assertions for the new wording/keys.
3. Keep wording consistent with the existing table's vocabulary (`infra-retry`, `failed`, `step`, `reason`, `attempt`).

**Key Files:**
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
- `tests/test_implement_docs_drive_recovery.py`

## Impact

An operator reading a stopped drive report can tell a transient provider failure from a real defect and knows the one-line config fix, without reading the drive source.

# Test-first contract: intake preserves refactor identity markers

## Summary

Define, as failing-first tests, the contract that intake's draft application step preserves the `Refactor-Finding-Key:`, `Refactor-Fingerprint:` and `Refactor-Affected-Lines:` lines already present in a refactor item's description — before the implementation in the sibling feature lands. Parent: `SA-0MWL5PKM5005QS9C` AC1, AC2, AC5.

## Test-first convention

Matches the existing repo precedent (`SA-0MWE1DXPW00846UV`, `tests/test_refactor/test_dedupe_identity.py`): tests are written first and each test probes for the *specific* helper/constant the implementation feature introduces. A test whose helper has not landed yet skips with an explicit `not yet implemented (SA-<impl-id>)` reason, so this item's changed-scope gate stays green while the implementation item is still open, and the implementation item's gate turns the same tests green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New test module `skill/intake/tests/test_intake_marker_preservation.py` exists and is collected by the project test runner.
- The module defines tests for all four marker-preservation scenarios: (a) markers present in the current description are present in the applied description, (b) an item with no markers gains none, (c) re-running the merge is idempotent (no duplicated marker lines), (d) a non-refactor item's description is byte-identical after the merge.
- Additional cases are covered: marker preservation when the draft has no leading `#`/`##` heading (markers go to the very top), and markers embedded mid-line (quoted inside prose) are **not** preserved.
- Assertions compare exact marker lines (`Refactor-Finding-Key: <code>:<path>` etc.) and assert the preserved block sits before the draft's first `##` heading, not merely "somewhere in the text".
- Each test that requires a not-yet-landed helper calls `pytest.skip("<reason> (SA-<impl-id>)")` via an import-capability guard, so the module passes on its own before the implementation exists.
- `python3 skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py --scope changed` (via the test skill) passes.

## Minimal implementation

- Add the new test module following the style of `skill/intake/tests/test_intake_scripts_cwd.py` (repo-root `sys.path` insertion, `mock.patch` of `shared.status_lifecycle._find_worklog_dir_by_prefix` for hermetic worklog resolution, `mock.patch` of `intake.scripts.intake.run_wl` to capture the `wl update` invocation).
- Provide a small local fixture factory that writes a draft markdown file to `tmp_path` and a fake `wl show <id> --json` payload for the current description.
- Guard imports with a per-helper capability probe, in the style of `tests/test_refactor/test_dedupe_identity.py::_require`.

## Key Files

- `skill/intake/tests/test_intake_marker_preservation.py` — new contract test module (all preservation cases).
- `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py` — read-only reference for the `cmd_finish` / `_run_wl_update_description` seams the tests target.
- `skill/intake/tests/test_intake_scripts_cwd.py` — style/mocking reference.

## Constraints

- No production code changes in this item — tests only.
- Tests must not shell out to a real `wl` store; the store is mocked or a `tmp_path` worklog is used.
- Follow `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`: no self-referential simulations, no duplicates of existing coverage.

## Dependencies

None — created first (test-first ordering).

## Deliverables

- `skill/intake/tests/test_intake_marker_preservation.py` with the contract above.

# Preserve refactor identity markers when intake applies its draft

## Summary

Stop `/skill:intake` from destroying a refactor item's machine-readable identity: before `cmd_finish` applies the intake draft with `wl update --description-file`, carry over every `Refactor-Finding-Key:`, `Refactor-Fingerprint:` and `Refactor-Affected-Lines:` line already in the item's description and place them at the top of the new description. Parent: `SA-0MWL5PKM5005QS9C` AC1, AC2, AC6.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `intake.py finish <id> --description-file <draft>` writes a description that contains every refactor marker line present in the item's pre-finish description, verbatim, positioned immediately below the draft's leading heading (or at the very top when the draft has no heading).
- Re-running `finish` with the same draft is idempotent: each marker line appears exactly once.
- An item whose description has no marker lines gains none, and an item that is not refactor-created (`Refactor` tag absent and no markers present) is left with the draft applied unchanged.
- Marker extraction only matches the documented marker set at line start (`Refactor-Finding-Key:`, `Refactor-Fingerprint:`, `Refactor-Affected-Lines:`); a marker string quoted mid-line in prose is never treated as a marker.
- The current description is read through the shared `run_wl` helper (worklog-dir resolution respected, caller cwd independent), and a read failure fails closed to "no markers" rather than aborting the intake.
- The applied description is written from a temporary file (no mutation of the caller's draft file), and `finish`'s existing terminal transition (`open` + `intake_complete` + explicit `assignee=""`) and its failure-reset path are unchanged.
- The test module from the sibling test-first item (`skill/intake/tests/test_intake_marker_preservation.py`) passes with no skips.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` § Finish and `docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md` document marker preservation (what is preserved, why — duplicate suppression, and that nothing is synthesised).
- `python3 skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py --scope changed` (via the test skill) passes.

### Parent AC coverage (parent SA-0MWL5PKM5005QS9C)

- Parent AC1: Intake `finish` preserves every `Refactor-Finding-Key:`, `Refactor-Fingerprint:` and `Refactor-Affected-Lines:` line present in the item's existing description and places them near the top of the new intake description (the same leading-block convention the refactor skill uses), before the draft is applied.
- Parent AC2: Marker preservation is idempotent and side-effect free: re-running intake does not duplicate marker lines, an item whose description has no markers gains none, and non-refactor items are unchanged.
- Parent AC6: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/intake/SKILL.md`, `skill/refactor/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Minimal implementation

- Add pure helpers in `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py`: `extract_refactor_markers(text) -> list[str]` (line-start, documented markers only, order preserving, de-duplicated) and `merge_markers_into_draft(draft, markers) -> str` (inserts missing markers below the first leading heading, else at the top; idempotent by construction because only absent lines are inserted).

# Test-first contract: legacy identity fallback in the refactor duplicate guard

## Summary

Define, as failing-first tests, the contract that the refactor pre-creation duplicate guard recognises a non-terminal **marker-less legacy** refactor item by reconstructing its `<code>:<repository-relative path>` identity from its title/description. This is the damage-repair half: items already rewritten by intake cannot regain markers, so they must still suppress duplicate filings. Parent: `SA-0MWL5PKM5005QS9C` AC3, AC4, AC5.

## Test-first convention

Extends `tests/test_refactor/test_dedupe_identity.py` in the established style: each test probes for the specific helper the implementation feature introduces and skips with `not yet implemented (SA-0MWLLKNJU0015592)` while that helper is absent, so this item's changed-scope gate is green before the implementation lands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/test_refactor/test_dedupe_identity.py` gains a legacy-fallback section covering a **match**: a non-terminal, marker-less item whose description carries structured `- **Code:** \`S112\`` and `- **File:** \`skill/x.py\`` fields is returned by the duplicate guard for the smell `S112` in `skill/x.py`.
- A **title-only** legacy match is covered: a non-terminal marker-less item titled `Refactor: Long Method in skill/x.py` whose description records the rule/smell type is matched by the same identity.
- Negative cases are covered and assert `None`: a different rule code on the same file; the same rule code on a different file; a path that merely contains the target path as a substring (e.g. `skill/x.py.bak` vs `skill/x.py`); a terminal (`completed` / `deleted`) legacy item; an item whose description carries neither a code nor a path (unidentifiable).
- The tests assert the guard performs **exact** comparison (no substring matching) and that a marker-carrying item still takes precedence over any legacy reconstruction.
- The query used to find legacy candidates returns the full refactor family (`Refactor` tag) rather than only `Refactor-Finding-Key:` items, and the test asserts a marker-less item is actually seen by the lookup (i.e. the lookup, not just the parser, is covered).
- `python3 skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py --scope changed` (via the test skill) passes.

### Parent AC coverage (parent SA-0MWL5PKM5005QS9C)

- Parent AC4: The legacy fallback creates no false positives: a different rule code on the same file, the same rule on a different file, a terminal item, and an item that cannot be identified all remain non-matches.

## Minimal implementation

- Add a `TestLegacyIdentityFallback` section to `tests/test_refactor/test_dedupe_identity.py` (or a new sibling module `tests/test_refactor/test_dedupe_legacy_fallback.py` if the existing module becomes unwieldy — decide at implementation time, keeping the existing module's contract intact).
- Reuse the existing mocking style in that module: patch the `wl list` subprocess call with canned JSON payloads for the two queries (marker query and `--tags Refactor` query).
- Provide a fixture factory building canned worklog items (`id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `tags`) per case.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_refactor/test_dedupe_identity.py` — the identity/dedupe contract module this section extends.
- `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — `_find_existing_worklog_item` is the function under test.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/consolidate_duplicates.py` — existing legacy-identity parsing (`_item_identity`, `_LEGACY_CODE_RE`, `_LEGACY_FILE_RE`, `_TITLE_IN_RE`) the tests must stay semantically consistent with.

## Constraints

- No production code changes in this item — tests only.
- No real `wl` store access; subprocess calls are mocked.
- Follow `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`: no self-referential simulations, no duplicates of existing coverage.

## Dependencies

None — created before the implementation item (test-first ordering). Independent of the intake-half children.

## Deliverables

- Legacy-fallback contract tests (match, title-only match, code mismatch, path mismatch, substring-safety, terminal, unidentifiable).

# Add a legacy identity fallback to the refactor duplicate guard

## Summary

Make the refactor pre-creation duplicate guard see items that lost their identity markers, so an intake-rewritten refactor item still suppresses a repeat filing. When `_find_existing_worklog_item()` finds no `Refactor-Finding-Key:` for a candidate item, reconstruct `<code>:<repository-relative path>` from its title/description and compare it exactly. Parent: `SA-0MWL5PKM5005QS9C` AC3, AC4, AC6.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `_find_existing_worklog_item()` consults the whole refactor family, not only marker-carrying items: after the existing `wl list "Refactor-Finding-Key:"` lookup it performs one `wl list --tags Refactor --json` lookup for legacy candidates (a marker-only query can never return a marker-less item).
- For a candidate with no `Refactor-Finding-Key:` marker the guard reconstructs the identity from, in order: structured `- **Code:**` / `- **File:**` description fields, the `## Code Smell:` heading plus `- **File:**`, and the `Refactor: <smell> in <path>` title (path from the title's `in <path>` suffix, code from the recorded rule/smell). The reconstructed identity is normalised and compared **exactly** with the smell's identity — no substring matching anywhere.
- Both halves must be established for a match; when either the code or the path cannot be determined the candidate is a non-match (fail open — a genuinely new finding is still filed).
- A marker-carrying item is always matched via its marker; the legacy reconstruction is only a fallback, and its result never overrides or contradicts a parsed marker.
- Terminal (`completed` / `deleted`) legacy items remain non-matches, and a legacy item whose reconstructed path differs from, or merely contains, the target path (`skill/x.py.bak` vs `skill/x.py`) never matches.
- The legacy parsing is **shared** with `skill/refactor/scripts/consolidate_duplicates.py` (extract the field/title parsing into one helper in `workitem_creation.py` and have the consolidation tool import it, or an equivalently single-source arrangement) so the two cannot drift; `tests/test_refactor/test_consolidate_duplicates.py` keeps passing unchanged.
- The legacy lookup is best-effort: a failing or slow `wl` call logs and returns "no legacy match" rather than raising, preserving the guard's existing fail-open behaviour.
- The contract tests from the sibling test-first item (`tests/test_refactor/test_dedupe_identity.py` legacy-fallback section) pass with no skips.
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` § Finding identity and dedupe and `docs/refactor.md` § 4 (Work Item Creation for Pre-existing Smells) document the legacy fallback (when it applies, exactness, fail-open, and that legacy items are matched but never rewritten to add markers).
- `python3 skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py --scope changed` (via the test skill) passes.

### Parent AC coverage (parent SA-0MWL5PKM5005QS9C)

- Parent AC3: The refactor pre-creation duplicate guard (`_find_existing_worklog_item`) matches a non-terminal marker-less legacy item by reconstructing its `<code>:<repository-relative path>` identity from the item's title/description (structured `- **Code:**` plus `- **File:**` fields, or the `Refactor: <smell> in <path>` title plus the recorded rule), using exact normalised comparison and no substring matching, so items already damaged by an earlier intake rewrite do not breed duplicates.
- Parent AC6: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/intake/SKILL.md`, `skill/refactor/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Minimal implementation

- In `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py`, add a shared pure parser `parse_legacy_item_identity(item) -> str | None` returning a raw `<code>:<path>` (or `{code, path}`) from the legacy structured fields/title; name and document the three-source precedence.
- Add `_find_legacy_worklog_item(smell, repo_root)` mirroring `_find_existing_audit_twin`'s shape (subprocess `wl list --tags Refactor --json`, 15 s timeout, "fail open" on any error), skipping items that carry a marker and terminal items, and matching on normalised exact identity.
- Call it from `_find_existing_worklog_item` after the marker loop, before returning `None`; keep the repeat-comment / line-union behaviour in `create_smell_work_item` working for a legacy match (a legacy item's `Refactor-Affected-Lines` may be absent — an appended repeat comment is still correct, a silent dedupe must not crash on an empty tracked line set).
- Update `skill/refactor/scripts/consolidate_duplicates.py::_item_identity` to delegate to the shared parser, keeping its main-root path normalisation.
- Update the module docstring/`__all__`-style documentation list in `workitem_creation.py` and the refactor SKILL.md section.

## Key Files

- `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — shared legacy parser plus `_find_existing_worklog_item` / new `_find_legacy_worklog_item`.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/consolidate_duplicates.py` — delegate legacy parsing to the shared helper.
- `tests/test_refactor/test_dedupe_identity.py` — the contract written by the test-first sibling.
- `tests/test_refactor/test_consolidate_duplicates.py` — must keep passing.
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — duplicate-prevention documentation.
- `docs/refactor.md` — user-facing § 4 work-item-creation documentation.

## Constraints

- Do not change the marker format or identity semantics (`<code>:<repository-relative path>`, line excluded).
- Never rewrite a legacy item to add markers — matching is read-only.
- No `wl` schema change, no bulk migration; the historical duplicates stay the consolidation tool's job.
- Do not widen the lookup into non-refactor items (tag-gated), so an unrelated description mentioning a file path cannot suppress a real finding.
- Validate through the test skill / changed-scope gate; no ad-hoc test runs.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the legacy-fallback test-first contract item.

## Deliverables

- Legacy identity fallback in the duplicate guard, shared parser, and updated refactor documentation.

## Summary

Prove the two halves join up: after `/skill:intake` has rewritten a refactor item's description (marker preserved by half 1, or already lost on a legacy item and recovered by half 2), the next refactor scan files **no** duplicate. Parent: `SA-0MWL5PKM5005QS9C` AC5, AC7.

- An integration test drives the real intake `finish` path (draft file → `cmd_finish`) against a refactor item that carries all three markers, then feeds the resulting description into the refactor duplicate guard and asserts the guard returns that item instead of creating a new one.
- A second integration case covers the pre-damaged legacy item: a description with no markers (intake-style prose plus `- **Code:**` / `- **File:**` or a `Refactor: <smell> in <path>` title) is recognised by the guard through the legacy fallback.
- A control case proves no over-suppression: the same flow with a *different* rule code files a new item; a terminal legacy item does not suppress.
- The test exercises production code end-to-end (intake helper → rendered description → guard), not a re-implementation of either half; `wl` interactions are injected/mocked and no real worklog store is mutated.

### Parent AC coverage (parent SA-0MWL5PKM5005QS9C)

- Parent AC5: Tests cover marker preservation (markers present, markers absent, idempotent re-run, non-refactor item), the legacy fallback (match, code mismatch, path mismatch, absent item), and an end-to-end case where an intake-rewritten refactor item suppresses a repeat filing.

# Audit code-quality scan lints gitignored paths (explicit scope bypasses `.gitignore`)

## Problem

The audit's automated code-quality scan files lint findings against files the
project's `.gitignore` excludes — notably `.worklog/` scratch scripts and
worktree copies — even though no committable remediation exists for them. The
2026-10-29 llm-project reviews produced exactly this: three items filed against
`.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py` (one `critical` F401, one `high` E401,
one `medium` I001), each of which could only be closed as a verification-only
no-op.

Impact: scheduling noise in every audited project, and a `critical`-tagged
phantom competes with real defects in `wl next`. Worse, the loop is
self-sustaining — a filed child repeats the offending path in its
description/`Key Files`, which re-enters the item-derived scan scope on the next
audit.

## Root cause (verified, not assumed)

1. `_resolve_code_quality_scope` (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`)
   resolves an **explicit file scope**: first the git changed-file list
   (`git diff --name-only HEAD` + `git status --porcelain=v1`), then the item's
   committed touched files / `Key Files` (`_resolve_touched_files`).
2. `_filter_code_quality_scope` bounds that scope by project containment and
   nested repositories only (SA-0MVPDTSRV0049KW2). It applies **no `.gitignore`
   check** — there is no `git check-ignore` anywhere in `skill/audit/scripts/`
   or `skill/code_review/scripts/`.
3. `run_ruff` (`skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py`, `_run_ruff_check`)
   therefore receives the gitignored path **as an explicit argument**, and ruff
   lints explicitly-passed paths regardless of `.gitignore`, even with
   `--force-exclude`. Probe (2026-11-18, `~/projects/llm`, repo `.venv` ruff),
   against a scratch file under the gitignored `.worklog/analysis/`:

   - `git check-ignore -v` → `.gitignore:6:.worklog/`
   - `ruff check <path> --extend-exclude '**/*.ts,**/*.yaml' --force-exclude --output-format json`
     → **3 findings** (F401 ×2, I001) — the audit's command shape
   - `ruff check .worklog/analysis/` (directory recursion) → `All checks passed!`

   So only the explicit-path scope is defective; ruff's own traversal already
   honours `.gitignore`.

A gitignore-aware filter already exists: `refactor.path_filters.filter_scannable_paths`
(default `.worklog` exclusion plus a batched `git check-ignore --no-index`).
Probe: `filter_scannable_paths(['.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py',
'proxy/server.py'], repo_root='~/projects/llm')` → `['proxy/server.py']`.

## Acceptance Criteria

Test-first: AC1–AC5 are pinned by failing tests written before the fix.

1. `_filter_code_quality_scope` drops any path matched by the project's
   `.gitignore`, for **both** scope sources (git changed-file list and
   item-derived touched/`Key Files`). Verified by a unit test on a temporary git
   repository whose `.gitignore` excludes a directory that holds a `.py` file.
2. A tracked-but-gitignored file is dropped too (the `--no-index` case), while a
   tracked in-scope file in the same list is retained — no over-filtering.
3. A merely **untracked but not ignored** file is retained, because an audit of
   in-progress work must still lint the item's brand-new files.
4. Gitignore filtering uses **one batched** `git check-ignore` call (no
   per-file subprocess) and degrades gracefully — on git failure / non-repository
   root the paths are kept and a warning is logged, so a git problem never
   silently empties the audit's lint scope.
5. Existing scope behaviour is preserved: containment inside the project root,
   nested-repository exclusion, the dropped-paths stderr warning, input order,
   and the `_FILE_SCOPE_MAX_FILES` cap.
6. The helper is **reused**, not reimplemented: the audit calls
   `refactor.path_filters.filter_scannable_paths` (or its batched
   `git check-ignore` core) rather than adding a second gitignore
   implementation.
7. A gitignored-path finding is never filed: with the scope fixed, a scan of
   `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py` in `~/projects/llm` emits zero
   findings — recorded as command + output on this item (no severity demotion
   path is added; the scope filter is the single gate).
8. `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` documents the code-quality scan-scope
   contract (project containment → nested repository → `.gitignore`) as the
   documented scope assertion, and the `_run_ruff_check` docstring records that
   `--force-exclude` does **not** cover explicitly-passed gitignored paths.
9. The audit and code-review suites pass via the test skill, plus the full suite
   at the dev-push gate.

## Implementation sketch

1. Write the red tests first in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_code_quality_scope.py`
   (tmp git repo + `git init`, in the style of the existing containment tests).
2. Extend `_filter_code_quality_scope` to run the surviving paths through
   `refactor.path_filters.filter_scannable_paths` (with
   `require_source_extension=False`, preserving the existing `.py`-narrowing in
   `_run_ruff_check`) before applying the nested-repository/containment bounds;
   keep the dropped-count stderr warning and extend its message to distinguish
   gitignored drops.
3. Re-run the probe scan against `~/projects/llm/.worklog/analysis/` and paste
   the result on this item (AC7 evidence).
4. Update `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` and the `_run_ruff_check`
   docstring (AC8).

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_filter_code_quality_scope` (fix
  site), `_resolve_code_quality_scope`, `_resolve_touched_files`.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_code_quality_scope.py` — regression tests.
- `skill/refactor/path_filters.py` — reused batched
  `git check-ignore --no-index` filtering.
- `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` — ruff invocation docstring (the
  `--force-exclude` limitation).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — documented scan-scope contract.

## Constraints

- No new third-party dependency; no new gitignore implementation.
- One batched git call; graceful degradation when git is unavailable.
- Merely untracked files must stay in scope (audits of in-progress work).
- No behaviour change beyond the gitignore exclusion.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the historical trigger for the 2026-10-29 findings could not be
  fully reconstructed from the log; the defect is reproducible on the current
  tree with the probe above, so the fix is justified regardless.
- **Risk:** an over-broad filter silently shrinks audit coverage — pinned by
  AC2/AC3 (tracked and untracked-not-ignored files retained).
- **Risk:** a cross-skill import (audit → refactor). Accepted by the producer
  (Q3 answer (a)); extraction into `skill/shared/` is the follow-up if a third
  caller appears.
- **Assumption (documented):** priority raised from the relocated item's `low` to
  `medium` because the defect files `critical`-severity noise in every audited
  project and self-perpetuates across items.

## Provenance

Relocated from the llm-project item `LP-0MVTKJ8KN0069TJV` (producer decision
2026-11-18, Q1 answer (a)): the defect lives in this repository's agent
infrastructure, so it is implemented and released here; the llm item is deleted
after relocation. Discovered while no-op-closing `LP-0MVTJXCN7000V3SA` (F401 on
`.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1:** "Where should the fix be implemented — a SorraAgents work item
  (relocate), or directly from the llm item with explicit permission to edit
  `skill/`?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-18):** Relocate; delete the llm item
  after relocation, and `wl sync` once this item is created. Final: relocate.
- **Q2:** "For a gitignored-path finding that still reaches the quality-epic
  filer, should nothing be filed, should it be filed `low` with an 'untracked
  scratch file' note, or both?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-18):** (a) — file
  nothing; the scope filter is the only gate (AC7). Final: (a).
- **Q3:** "May the audit reuse `refactor.path_filters.filter_scannable_paths`,
  extract the batched `git check-ignore` core into `skill/shared/`, or duplicate
  a minimal check?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-18):** (a) — reuse. Final:
  (a) (AC6).
- **Q4 (agent research):** "Does ruff already honour `.gitignore` for the
  explicit-path scope the audit uses?" — **Answer (probe 2026-11-18,
  `~/projects/llm`):** No; directory recursion passes, an explicitly-passed
  gitignored `.py` file still yields F401/I001 findings with `--force-exclude`.
- **Q5 (agent research):** "Is a gitignore-aware scan filter already available?"
  — **Answer (probe of `skill/refactor/path_filters.py`):** Yes; it drops
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py` and keeps `proxy/server.py`.
- **Q6 (agent research):** "Is this already covered by an existing item?" —
  **Answer (`wl search`, both stores):** No; `SA-0MVPDVXT90067E3M` fixed the

# Problem

`implement.py parent` / `implement.py drive` fail closed **before any session is
spawned** when the repository already holds ambient uncommitted work in the main
checkout or in other items' registered worktrees.
`_child_main_checkout_violation()` attributes that pre-existing dirt to a
never-spawned child whose own worktree is clean (zero commits ahead of `dev`),
because its "any other change surface holds changes" condition has no time
component. The only current exemption is the spawn-failure record, which exists
only after the driver has attempted a spawn and the session died
(SA-0MWGZ8NWP009QD8G) — it cannot apply to a child that will be spawned by the
very same `phase_parent` call.

Reproduction (2026-11-17, `llm` epic `LP-0MVVCO1N7004TNGY`): a dirty main
checkout plus four dirty sibling worktrees plus a startable child with an
existing clean worktree ⇒ `drive` spawns **0** sessions and reports every dirty
surface as the child's stray write.

# User story

As an operator driving an epic, I want `implement.py drive <epic>` to start the
next startable child even when the repository already holds unrelated
uncommitted work, so that a long-lived checkout with several items in flight
does not make every epic undriveable.

# Acceptance Criteria

- A regression test builds the incident shape over real git sandboxes (`shared.git_sandbox`): ≥1 dirty tracked path in the main checkout, ≥1 dirty registered sibling worktree, and a startable (`open`) child with an existing clean worktree holding zero commits ahead of `dev`; `phase_parent` reports the child startable (`next_child` set, implementation action) with `placement_violation` not True and `success` True.
- A regression test asserts `phase_drive` spawns the next startable child in that scenario through an injected fake `spawn_session` (no real Pi session), and its report does not name any unrelated sibling worktree as an offender.
- A regression test asserts the genuine case still fails closed: a child whose session baseline predates the write and which writes only into the main checkout — or only into another item's linked worktree — is still reported as `placement_violation: True` even when other pre-existing dirt is present.
- Existing sibling-stray detection tests in `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` are updated to establish a session baseline before the injected write, and all continue to pass.
- The regression tests are written first (TDD) and land green. `implement.py finish` refuses a red tree, so they ship in the same commit as the fix children (mirroring SA-0MWGZ8E7C001X2HA / SA-0MWGZ8NWP009QD8G).
- Full suite green at the dev-push gate (parent AC5) — the new regression tests and the existing suite pass together.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` — incident reproduction, drive-spawn assertion, genuine-stray preservation.

# Tests

1. Never-spawned child + dirty main checkout + dirty sibling worktrees ⇒ `phase_parent` reports startable, no violation (parent AC1).
2. `phase_drive` in that scenario spawns exactly one child session via the fake spawner and names no sibling as an offender (parent AC3).
3. Session-baselined child writes only into the main checkout ⇒ still a placement violation (parent AC2).
4. Session-baselined child writes only into a sibling worktree ⇒ still a placement violation (parent AC2).

# Impact

A driver can start the next child of an epic on a checkout that already holds other items' uncommitted work, instead of every epic becoming undriveable until that dirt is cleaned.
data.title: Test: ambient-dirt regression for a never-spawned child

# Problem

The snapshot primitive is only useful if a baseline is recorded **before** a
child's session can write and read back afterwards. Wire the baseline through
the `start` → `parent` → `drive` lifecycle and persist it under the child's
`.worklog/`, mirroring the durable spawn-failure record
(`<worktree>/.worklog/spawn-failure.json`, SA-0MWGZ8NWP009QD8G).

This child completes parent AC1 and AC3 end to end: a never-spawned child is
exempt (no session has run), and a spawned child's writes are attributable on
the next `parent` pass.

# User story

As an operator driving an epic, I want the driver to record where the repository
stood before each child session and to re-read that record afterwards, so that
only a session's own writes fail the chain.

# Acceptance Criteria

- `phase_start` records a session baseline for the child in `<worktree>/.worklog/` (a path every dirty-path helper excludes) before any session runs; the record disappears with the worktree.
- `phase_drive` refreshes the child's session baseline immediately **before** spawning each child session, so a session's writes are attributable on the next `phase_parent` pass.
- `phase_parent` supplies the persisted baseline to `_child_main_checkout_violation` at both call sites (the `skip-in-progress` path and the `implement` path); when no baseline exists it records an ambient one before checking, so pre-existing dirt is never attributed to a never-spawned child.
- The baseline record never counts as work: `_classify_child_worktree` still reports `CHILD_CLEAN` and `_has_worktree_changes` stays False after it is written.
- A missing, malformed, or foreign-child baseline fails open to the legacy guard (never silently exempts a child).
- Tests cover the drive spawn boundary (baseline written before a fake spawn and read by the next parent pass), the never-spawned exemption, and the `.worklog/` exclusion.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_start`, `phase_drive`, `phase_parent`, `record_session_baseline` / `read_session_baseline` (new helpers), `SPAWN_FAILURE_FILE` precedent.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` — lifecycle coverage.

# Tests

1. `phase_start` writes a baseline under `.worklog/`; the child stays `CHILD_CLEAN`.
2. `phase_drive` refreshes the baseline before the fake spawn; the next `phase_parent` sees a post-baseline write as a violation.
3. A never-spawned child with ambient dirt and no baseline records an ambient baseline and is reported startable (parent AC1).
4. An unreadable/foreign baseline falls back to the legacy guard.

# Impact

`drive` can hand off the next child of an epic on a checkout with unrelated in-flight work, and still fails closed the moment a spawned session writes outside its own worktree.
data.title: Fix: session-baseline lifecycle across start/parent/drive

# Problem

The placement-guard documentation and the implement skill reference describe the
guard only in terms of "a foreign change surface holds changes", with the
spawn-failure record as the sole exemption. They do not document the
baseline/threshold semantics that make pre-existing ambient dirt exempt, so an
operator reading the docs would still expect the guard to fire for unrelated
in-flight work.

# User story

As an `implement.py` maintainer or operator, I want the placement guard's
baseline semantics documented, so I can predict when ambient dirt is exempt and
when a genuine stray write still fails closed.

# Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (The placement guard section) documents that pre-existing/ambient dirt in the main checkout and in registered sibling worktrees is **not** a placement violation, and explains the baseline/threshold semantics (what is captured, when it is captured/refreshed, and what counts as a post-baseline write).
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` documents the same semantics for `_child_main_checkout_violation`, `phase_start`, `phase_parent` and `phase_drive`, including where the baseline record lives under `.worklog/`.
- The docs state that a genuine post-baseline write still fails closed and names the offending paths and the child's own worktree.
- The docs keep the existing spawn-failure exemption description consistent with the new baseline mechanism (no contradictory rules).

**Key Files:**
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — The placement guard section.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — spawn-failure evidence section and the `_child_main_checkout_violation` reference.

# Tests

- Documentation-only change; verified by the docs lint/tests that cover these files (no new behavioural tests).

# Impact

Operators and maintainers can predict when pre-existing in-flight work is exempt from the placement guard and can debug a refusal from the docs alone.

# Pre-commit hook guard sandbox tests

## Goal

As the implementer of the commit-time guard, I want a hermetic test that pins
exactly when `.githooks/pre-commit` must refuse and when it must stay silent, so
the guard can never regress into blocking legitimate work.

Test-first half of parent AC3. This item writes **tests only** — the hook itself
is the sibling item *Pre-commit hook refuses main-checkout dev commits*.

## Context

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` is the sanctioned sandbox: `fixture_git_env()`,
  `scrub_repository_overrides()`, `run_git()`. It strips inherited `GIT_*`
  overrides so a polluted session environment cannot leak into the fixture.
- `tests/test_githooks_portability.py` is the precedent for a throw-away repo
  built from the committed `.githooks/` with `core.hooksPath=.githooks`.
- `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` is the precedent for asserting the
  `scripts/install_pi.sh` wiring block itself.
- The guard target is narrow: **`dev` in the main checkout**. A linked worktree,
  a feature branch, `git merge --ff-only` and a `wl sync` commit must all pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new hermetic module `tests/test_pre_commit_main_checkout_guard.py` builds a
  throw-away repository from the committed `.githooks/` with
  `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, a bare local `origin` and a sandboxed `$HOME`; it
  never touches the real checkout, the real `$HOME` or the network.
- It asserts a commit on `dev` in the main checkout is **refused at commit time**:
  non-zero exit, `HEAD` unchanged, no new commit object, and the refusal message
  names the branch (`dev`), the main checkout path, the worktree requirement and
  the operator override.
- Zero-width proof: after the refused commit attempt the repository's commit
  count and `git rev-parse HEAD` are byte-identical to the pre-attempt values.
- It asserts the hook does **not** fire (exit 0, commit created) when:
  (a) the same commit runs inside a linked worktree (`git worktree add`);
  (b) the main checkout is on a feature branch;
  (c) `ALLOW_MAIN_CHECKOUT_DEV_COMMIT=1` is set (and the override announces
  itself on stderr so a deliberate hot-fix stays auditable).
- It asserts the two legitimate main-checkout movements still succeed: a
  `git merge --ff-only` fast-forward of `dev` (no commit object is created) and a
  `wl sync`-style commit performed inside a temporary linked worktree
  (`.worklog/tmp-worktree-*`, detached `HEAD`) — the shape
  `ContextHub/dist/sync/worktree.js::withTempWorktree` uses.
- The suite is environment-clean: the fixture uses `fixture_git_env()` /
  `scrub_repository_overrides()` so inherited `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` or
  `GIT_WORK_TREE` cannot influence a verdict.
- Tests are run only through the test skill (`run_tests.py`), never ad hoc; the
  new module passes once the hook item lands, and is red before it (the hook
  does not exist yet).

## Minimal implementation

- One test module, module-level docstring citing parent AC3 and the four
  negative cases, helper functions for "make a repo", "commit a file", "add a
  linked worktree".
- No production code, no changes to `.githooks/`, no changes to
  `scripts/install_pi.sh`.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_pre_commit_main_checkout_guard.py` (new)
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (reused)
- `tests/test_githooks_portability.py` (pattern to reuse)

## Dependencies

- None. Must be merged before *Pre-commit hook refuses main-checkout dev commits*.

## Deliverables

- The failing-first test module and a short note on the red→green transition.

# Commit-helper guard tests for audit and code-review

## Goal

As a producer, I want the three skill commit helpers pinned by hermetic tests, so
"refuse to commit on `dev` in the main checkout" cannot be silently dropped from
one of them — especially from the duplicate `skill/code_review/` directory.

Test-first half of parent AC1. Tests only; the hardening is the sibling items
*Shared main-checkout commit guard + audit hardening* and *Harden code-review
commit helper in both directories*.

## Context

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_commit_config_remediation` (≈14222)
  stages one config file and commits with `REMEDIATION_COMMIT_MESSAGE`, locally,
  no push. Returns the short sha or `None`; its call site (≈14439) records
  failures into `results["chore_failures"]`.
- `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py::_commit_changes` (≈425) and the
  duplicate `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` (≈641) run `git add .`
  + `git commit -m "Auto-fix: <linter> applied fixes"`. Both directories are
  live: `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` and
  `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` import `code_review`; `code-review` is
  the skill-facing package that owns `SKILL.md`.
- The shared detection verdict must agree with `.githooks/pre-commit`:
  main checkout ⟺ `git rev-parse --git-dir` == `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`;
  target branch ⟺ `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` == `dev`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Hermetic tests (built on `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`) cover
  `_commit_config_remediation` and `_commit_changes` in both code-review
  directories.
- Refusal case: on `dev` in the main checkout the helper makes **no commit** and
  leaves **no staged change** behind (the staging step never runs), and returns
  its failure sentinel (`None` / `False`).
- Positive cases preserved: in a linked worktree, and on a feature branch in the
  main checkout, each helper still commits a real change — pinned for both.
- `ALLOW_MAIN_CHECKOUT_DEV_COMMIT=1` makes every helper commit (consistent with
  the hook), and the override is logged so the deliberate act is traceable.
- Audit call site: a refusal is recorded in `results["chore_failures"]` with a
  message naming the worktree requirement and the work-item id, so the audit
  report states why the remediation was not committed — it is never silently
  dropped.
- The two code-review helper twins are parametrised in one test so they cannot
  drift apart again; an explicit assertion pins "both directories refuse
  identically".
- Unit tests for the new `skill/shared/commit_guard.py` detection helper
  (`is_main_checkout`, `current_branch`, `commit_refusal_reason`) cover the
  main-checkout, linked-worktree, feature-branch, detached-`HEAD` and override
  cases — so a shell and a Python verdict can never disagree.

## Minimal implementation

- One audit test module, one parametrised code-review test module, and one
  helper-unit test module (or a single module with three test classes).
- No production-code edits.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/tests/` (new module for `_commit_config_remediation`)
- `skill/code-review/tests/` and/or `skill/code_review/tests/` (new parametrised module)
- `skill/shared/tests/` (new `test_commit_guard.py`)
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (reused)

## Dependencies

- None. Must be merged before the two hardening items.

## Deliverables

- Red-first tests for all three helpers plus the shared guard primitive.

# Start refusal attribution tests

## Goal

As a producer, when `implement.py start` refuses because `dev` is not a pushed
tip, I want the refusal pinned by tests that name the owning work items, so
reconciliation is one step instead of a manual log trawl.

Test-first half of parent AC2. Tests only; the implementation is the sibling item
*Start refusal names owning work items*.

## Context

- `_resolve_start_base` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` ≈8021) produces
  `reason: local_dev_not_a_pushed_tip` and an opaque three-step warning
  (≈8123-8137). `phase_start` (≈12081-12110) posts a work-item comment naming
  only the two tips, then releases the claim to `open`.
- `WORK_ITEM_ID_RE = re.compile(r"\b([A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,9}-[A-Z0-9]{2,})\b")` at
  `implement.py` ≈1951 is the existing id pattern — reuse it, do not add a
  second one.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_start_base_resolution.py` already has
  `test_base_refuses_local_dev_with_unpushed_commits` (≈112) and
  `test_phase_start_refuses_a_worktree_from_unpushed_local_dev` (≈315); extend
  that module rather than starting a new one.
- Related work: SA-0MVY4SG8O001RSQF (open) establishes that commit **body**
  mentions are not ownership evidence — AC2 says *subject scan*, so ownership is
  resolved from the subject only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `skill/implement/tests/test_start_base_resolution.py` gains tests asserting the
  refusal names the owning work item(s) for commits whose **subject** contains an
  id (e.g. `fix: Wrap implicit string concatenation (SA-0MWDKRD8G008Z164)`).
- A commit with no id in its subject is reported as **unattributed** — never
  dropped and never silently attributed to the current work item.
- An id present only in the commit **body** does not make that item the owner
  (subject-scan-only contract, consistent with SA-0MVY4SG8O001RSQF).
- The report carries the attribution machine-readably (per-commit sha, subject,
  owning ids and an `unattributed` flag) under
  `report["steps"]["worktree_base"]`, so `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh` and
  future tooling do not have to re-parse prose.
- The `phase_start` work-item comment names the owning items, keeps the existing
  three-step remedy (inspect, verify, push or reset with operator confirmation)
  and points at the reconciliation helper.
- The refusal decision itself is unchanged: `worktree_refused is True`, no
  worktree created, claim released to `open` — the pushed-tip invariant stays
  exactly as it is.
- Fail-open coverage: an unreachable remote (fetch failure) still branches from
  local `dev`; attribution absence never turns a legitimate start into a refusal.
- Message bound: a long unpushed range is truncated with an explicit
  "… and N more" so the warning stays readable, and that truncation is tested.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend the existing module with attribution-specific tests and a helper that
  builds a repo with 3 unpushed commits (attributed, unattributed, body-only id).
- No production-code edits.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/tests/test_start_base_resolution.py` (extend)

## Dependencies

- None. Must be merged before *Start refusal names owning work items*.

## Deliverables

- Red-first attribution tests.

# Reconcile unpushed dev helper tests

## Goal

As a producer, I want the reconciliation helper's contract pinned by tests —
push by default, reset only on explicit confirmation — so recovery from a
poisoned `dev` can never destroy work by accident.

Test-first half of parent AC4. Tests only; the script and its documentation are
the sibling item *Reconcile unpushed dev helper script and docs*.

## Context

- The helper will live at `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh` and is documented
  in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (pushed-tip guarantees section,
  ≈2638).
- Existing precedents for testing a repository script hermetically:
  `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py`, `tests/test_cleanup_scripts.py`, and
  the sandbox helpers in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`.
- Push policy: pushes go to `dev` only — never `main`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new `tests/test_reconcile_unpushed_dev.py` builds a bare local `origin` plus
  a clone whose `dev` carries unpushed commits; no real checkout, `$HOME` or
  network is touched.
- Listing: output names each `origin/dev..dev` commit (short sha + subject) and
  its owning work item(s) parsed from the subject, with an explicit
  **unattributed** bucket.
- Default action is **push**: after a plain run, `origin/dev` advanced and local
  `dev` equals `origin/dev`.
- Reset is opt-in only: without the explicit confirmation flag the helper refuses,
  mutates nothing (both refs byte-identical) and names the flag; with it, the
  helper prints the commits it discards **before** discarding, then resets so
  local `dev` equals `origin/dev`.
- No-op path: when `dev` == `origin/dev` the helper exits 0 with a clear "nothing
  to reconcile" message and mutates nothing.
- `--dry-run` lists and mutates nothing; `--json` emits a machine-readable
  document (commits, owning items, unattributed) stable enough for automation.
- Safety refusals: running in a linked worktree or with `dev` not checked out is
  refused with an actionable message (the helper targets the main checkout).
- Failure safety: a failed push leaves local `dev` unchanged and exits non-zero.

## Minimal implementation

- One hermetic test module driving the script through `subprocess` with a
  sandboxed environment and a local bare remote.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_reconcile_unpushed_dev.py` (new)
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (reused)

## Dependencies

- None. Must be merged before *Reconcile unpushed dev helper script and docs*.

## Deliverables

- Red-first tests for the reconciliation helper.

# Hygiene check reports unpushed dev commits

## Goal

As a producer running periodic hygiene, I want `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` to warn
about committed-but-unpushed `dev` commits, so a poisoned `dev` is visible before
the next `start` refuses.

Optional hardening listed in the item's predicted key files; parent ACs do not
require it. Low priority — drop without prejudice if the producer prefers a
tighter scope.

## Context

- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh::check_dirty_checkout` (≈179) already warns about a
  dirty-though-not-committed main checkout, with a `--json` line
  `{"check":"dirty_checkout",…}`; it does not see committed-but-unpushed `dev`.
- The check must be offline-safe: compare against the existing
  `refs/remotes/origin/dev` tracking ref, never `git fetch`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new `check_unpushed_dev` reports, in human and `--json` form
  (`{"check":"unpushed_dev","status":"warning","commits":[…],"owning_items":[…]}`),
  every `origin/dev..dev` commit with its owning work item(s) and an
  `unattributed` bucket; exit status follows the existing convention (0 ok,

# Refactor skill injects finding comments into whatever checkout it runs in

## Problem

Discovered during intake of SA-0MWM8XZNI0028SRU (downtime workers commit directly
to `dev` in the main checkout).

The refactor skill writes `<!-- REFACTOR-<item-id> -->` markers directly into
source files in its current working directory. When a downtime-dispatched session
runs it with `--cwd <main checkout root>`, it dirties the shared main checkout
without committing anything.

Observed 2026-11-18 ~16:08-16:12 during a concurrent refactor session: the main
checkout was dirtied with `<!-- REFACTOR-SA-… -->` injections in
`scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`, `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py`,
`skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/config.py`,
`skill/implement/tests/test_cleanup_worktree_action.py` and
`skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py` (plus
`.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`).

This is a **second main-checkout mutation surface** distinct from the
direct-commit path tracked in SA-0MWM8XZNI0028SRU: refactor does not commit, but
a dirty checkout `gate-refused` a concurrent pre-push (the same class of damage —
it blocks other sessions' pushes and worktree creation).

## Relation to the parent item

- Parent SA-0MWM8XZNI0028SRU covers **commits** on `dev` in the main checkout
  (skill commit helpers, the `.githooks/pre-commit` guard, `start` attribution,
  `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh`).
- This item covers **uncommitted writes** by the refactor skill. Its commit-time
  guard does not fire (no commit is made), so it needs its own fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The refactor skill refuses to inject finding comments when its target root is
  the main checkout (detected as `git rev-parse --git-dir` ==
  `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, the same rule as the pre-commit guard), and
  reports an actionable message pointing at the worktree requirement.
- Existing behaviour is preserved in a linked worktree and on a feature branch.
- A `git_sandbox` test pins both the refusal (main checkout unchanged, no
  markers written) and the worktree/feature-branch success path.
- Documentation states that refactor must run in a worktree, cross-referencing
  `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`.

## Impact

A dispatched refactor session can no longer dirty the shared main checkout,
which today blocks concurrent pre-push gates and worktree creation.

## Plan

Decomposed into five child work items, test-first and dependency-ordered:

| # | Work item | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Test: shared is_main_checkout() unit tests | Pin the main-checkout detection rule (`git rev-parse --git-dir` == `--git-common-dir`) |
| 2 | Implement: shared is_main_checkout() helper | One shared predicate in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` next to `main_checkout_root()` |
| 3 | Test: refactor main-checkout refusal and worktree success | `git_sandbox` tests pinning the refusal **and** the preserved worktree/feature-branch path |
| 4 | Implement: refactor main-checkout write refusal | Pipeline pre-flight guard + injection-level defence in depth |
| 5 | Docs: refactor must run in a worktree | `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` plus `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` |

Dependency chain: 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 (each implementation item depends on the test
item that pins it).

### Design decisions

- **One detection rule, one implementation.** The guard reuses the
  pre-commit/pre-push rule and is exposed once as
  `git_sandbox.is_main_checkout(path)`; the refactor skill does not re-implement
  git plumbing.
- **Fail fast, before any write.** The guard runs at the start of
  `refactor_pipeline`, before linter auto-fix (ruff/eslint `--fix` also write
  files in place) and before work-item creation. The refusal test can only
  assert "main checkout unchanged" if auto-fix is prevented too.
- **Defence in depth.** `inject_refactor_comment()` also refuses when the target
  file's repository root is the main checkout, so a caller that bypasses the
  pipeline still cannot mark files.
- **`--dry-run` is exempt** — it writes nothing, and read-only inspection of
  the main checkout stays possible.
- **Not in a git work tree → never refuse** (predicate returns `False`), so the
  skill keeps working outside git.
- **Vertical slice note:** effort is Small, so the change is phased as
  test→implementation pairs (shared helper, then refactor behaviour) followed by
  docs; each phase is independently landable and gated by its preceding test
  item. No horizontal layering.

### Effort and risk

Small effort (O=3h, M=6h, P=12h → 6.5h expected, 10.5h with overheads), Medium
risk (7/25; main driver is a false-positive refusal breaking legitimate runs,
mitigated by delegating to the existing git-plumbing rule, exempting
`--dry-run`, and testing the worktree success path).

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-18: Initial decomposition (5 children in a test-first dependency
  chain), effort/risk estimated, AC coverage review at 100% (`proceed`).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Seed context: bug item, priority medium, stage `intake_complete` at planning
start, no children, no prior Appendix entries. Discovered during intake of
SA-0MWM8XZNI0028SRU (downtime workers commit directly to `dev` in the main
checkout); related, non-overlapping items reviewed: SA-0MWE1E4GQ004E1JG
(marker identity, completed), SA-0MVXVBYXI000QMXM and SA-0MVXVC127009T0NP
(pre-push guard failure paths, completed), SA-0MW5KKEHL005BR0L (marker
cross-wiring, open). No existing or completed item covers this refusal.

**Producer interview:** none required — the acceptance criteria already pin the
detection rule, the refusal behaviour, the test requirement and the
documentation requirement. Duplicate-work check performed; no overlapping
completed item found.

**OPEN QUESTION (to: producer, non-blocking)** — AC2 reads "Existing behaviour
is preserved in a linked worktree and on a feature branch." Under the stated
detection rule, a feature branch checked out **in the main checkout** is still
the main checkout (`git-dir` == `git-common-dir`) and would therefore be
refused. The plan assumes "feature branch" means the normal agent flow — a
feature branch inside a linked worktree created by `implement.py start` — and
preserves that path. Why it matters: the alternative reading (allow the main
checkout when the branch is not `dev`) needs a different detection rule than
the one AC1 prescribes. Assumption adopted; nothing is blocked.

**Decision (agent, from the item text)** — the refusal is fail-fast at pipeline
start rather than a per-injection skip, because AC3 requires the refusal test to
assert "main checkout unchanged", which is only true when auto-fix writes are
prevented as well as marker injection.

**Decision (agent)** — the predicate lives in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`
beside `main_checkout_root()`/`is_worktree_git_dir()` so the commit-helper
guard items (SA-0MWMCVFXB0096UG5, SA-0MWMCVNK0003QVW8) reuse one rule instead
of growing a third copy.

**Observed at planning time (evidence, not a work item)** — the main checkout
was dirty with exactly the described artefacts (`scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`,
`skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py`,
`skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/config.py`,
`skill/implement/tests/test_cleanup_worktree_action.py`,
`skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py`,
`.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`), a live reproduction by a concurrent
dispatched refactor session. The planning session made no changes to those
files.
